summary: New Delhi- 110003, India Respondent Parties Present: Shri Buddy A. Ranganathan, Advocate, CPPA Shri K.R. Sasiprabhu, Advocate, CPPA Shri Gaurav Thakur, Advocate, CPPA Shri Vishnu Sharma, Advocate, CPPA Shri Manan Shishodia, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Shefali Tripathi, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Kavya Agarwal, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Namrata Rastogi, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Namrata Saraogi, Advocate, CPPA Ms. Vidhatri Deoli, Advocate, CPPA Shri Vijay Valsan, Advocate, CPPA आदेश/ ORDER The Petitioner, Captive Power Producers Association (CPPA), is an association of industries in Maharashtra and Gujarat. The members of the Petitioner Association have installed captive generation plants in their industries in these states and meet their energy requirements through captive-produced power. These captive power plants of the Petitioner are recognised as ‘co-generation’ plants under the Electricity Act, 2003. 2. The Respondent, Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), is a Ministry of the Government of India. The salutary objective of MNRE is to develop and deploy new and renewable energy to supplement the Country's energy requirements. 3. The present petition is filed by the Petitioner, CPPA, seeking revision in the methodology evolved by the Commission vide its order dated 18.02.2020 in Suo Motu Petition No. 12/SM/2019 for estimation of electricity generated from biomass in a co-generation power plant. 4. Petitioner has made the following prayers: Order in Petition No. 110/MP/2024 Page 2 of 9 13. Further, the Petitioner relied upon a catena of judicial decisions in support of its submissions. In this regard, reliance was placed on the judgments of the Supreme Court in UPPCL v. NTPC Ltd., (2009) 6 SCC 235, to submit that the Commission has the power to modify/ revisit the methodology and on the judgment of the APTEL in Ratnagiri Gas and Power Private Ltd. v. CERC, 2011 SCC Appeal No. 130 of 2009, where it was held that the Commission has the power to relax and modify when a Regulation in its application leads to injustice and undue hardship. The Commission also relied on the judgment of the APTEL in NTPC Ltd. v. AP Transmission Co. Ltd., wherein it was submitted that where reasonable grounds exist to revisit an order, the Commission ought to do so. Analysis and Decision 14. The Commission has heard the counsel for the Petitioner and considered the submissions, and has carefully perused the records. The Commission also notes that no one appeared on behalf of the Respondent during the hearing, nor did they make any written submissions in the matter. 15. Brief facts of the case: The Commission, vide its Order dated 18.02.2020 in Petition No. 12/SM/2019, specified the methodology for estimating the energy generated from biomass in biomass co-fired coal-based thermal power plants, including captive power plants and co-generation plants, which continues to be in force. As per the Petitioner (CPPA), the Commission, in the said Order, recognised that in conventional coal-based power plants, the entire heat generated from coal and biomass is used to generate power. However, in co-generation plants, only part of the heat is used to generate power. Under these circumstances, the Petitioner submitted that the methodology needs to be revisited in light of the data available for the past three years, which demonstrated that it is not suitable for co-generation plants, as it created inequality of treatment and unequal benefits for RPO compliance. Therefore, the Petitioner suggested a methodology and sought revision of the said methodology for estimating electricity generated from biomass in biomass co-fired thermal power plants, particularly in respect of co-generation plants. 16. The Commission notes that the only issue that arises for consideration is whether the methodology specified by the Commission vide its Order dated 18.02.2020 in Suo Motu Petition No. 12/SM/2019 for estimation of electricity generated from biomass in Order in Petition No. 110/MP/2024 Page 7 of 9 20. Further, as per the contention of the Petitioner that the methodology specified by the Commission vide Order dated 18.02.2020 should be revisited on the basis of data available for the past three years, the Commission notes that the Petitioner has not placed on record any data covering the said three-year period. The Petitioner has furnished an illustration supporting its suggested methodology for estimating the energy generated from biomass in co-generation plants, based on one month’s actual data from one of its members’ co-generation plants. However, such illustration does not, by itself, establish that the methodology specified vide Order dated 18.02.2020 is inappropriate for co- generation plants or warrants revision. 21. The Petitioner has also relied upon a catena of judicial decisions and contended that the Commission possesses regulatory power to revisit its earlier determination. The Commission recognises that it may revisit a methodology where the material placed on record warrants such reconsideration. In the present case, as noted above, the Commission already considered the specific distinction concerning co-generation plants while framing the methodology in the Order dated 18.02.2020. Accordingly, the Commission finds no sufficient basis to deviate from the methodology specified in the said Order. 22. The prayers of the Petitioner in the instant Petition are, therefore, rejected. 23. Petition No. 110/MP/2024 is disposed of in terms of the above.
